1.title: Agricultural flood risk
1.body: This map shows how much of Moldova's agricultural land is exposed to fluvial (river) flooding, nationwide. Pick a return period, then click a field or a raion to see how much land falls within the floodplain.

2.title: Built entirely on open data
2.body: Every layer comes from open, auditable data:

3.title: Open, auditable, serverless
3.body: The app is fully open-source and cloud-native — there is no backend. The large data (flood rasters and field boundaries) are hosted on Source Cooperative and served straight from a CDN. Anyone can audit every step.

4.title: Reproducible for any country
4.body: Because the data and code are open, this map can be re-run for any country in the world — the only real obstacle is compute. Other layers, such as building footprints, can be swapped in with minimal effort.

headline.stat_template: {pct} of mapped agricultural land falls within the 1-in-{rp} floodplain

rp.label: Return period
rp.info: The return period tells you how rare a flood of a given size is. RP100 is a flood expected on average once every 100 years. Put another way, it has about a 1% chance of happening in any given year.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.jrc: JRC GloFAS flood hazard v2.1.2, 90 m fluvial (CC BY 4.0)
sources.ftw: Fields of The World — field boundaries; our exposure is computed from these (CC BY 4.0)

eal.title: Expected annual loss
eal.info:
This is how much farmland floods in a typical year, averaged over the long run. In most years less floods. In rare, bad years far more floods. Add all those years together and divide, and you get the figure above.

The return-period buttons show one scenario at a time: a 1-in-100-year flood, a 1-in-500-year flood, and so on. The figure here already blends all of them, each counted by how often it happens. That is why it stays the same when you press a different button. It sums up every scenario, not any single one.

In any given year the real flooded area will be higher or lower. Often much lower, sometimes far higher.
